decisions.statement: A rule set declares its own fields.
A condition naming a field the rule set did not declare is refused.
A field's type comes from a set the engine closes.
A rule set invents no field type.
A rule set chooses among the engine's types rather than adding a type.
A field's type decides which comparisons the field takes.
One comparison spelled alike over two types is two comparisons.
Nothing refuses a condition pairing a field with a comparison that field refuses.
There is no boolean field type.
A field with two values is an enum with two values.
A date field has a calendar date.
A date field takes `is` and `on or after`.
A date is no number.
A date field's comparison takes in the day the comparison names.
An enum field has a value from a set the rule set names.
An enum field takes `is`.
An enum's set is complete.
A list field has many values at once.
A list field takes `contains`.
A list's `contains` asks membership.
A list's `contains` asks no substring.
A list names the type the list's members have.
A number field has a count or an amount.
A number field takes `is` and `is above`.
A number field's values divide the line into one more piece than the values.
A text field has a run of characters.
A text field takes `is` and `starts with` and `ends with` and `contains`.
No text field takes `contains`.
A normalizer turns a run of raw text into one value out of a bounded set.
A normalizer is a list of patterns.
A normalizer's pattern names one value.
A normalizer is declared as data rather than written as code.
A normalizer's pattern is a run of characters.
A normalizer's pattern is no regular expression.
The longest pattern the text has names the text's value.
The first pattern alphabetically names the value where two patterns tie.
Text holding no pattern takes a value of its own.
No rule set has a field a normalizer fills.

definition: one property of what a rule set applies to, that a condition can name
